headline: Slower deliveries do not meaningfully increase item return rates.
question: Do slower deliveries lead to more returns?

report.closing_summary: Focus improvement efforts on high-return categories and platforms rather than delivery speed.
report.confidence_justification: Capped below HIGH — a trust advisory fired on the evidence: every value in this result is identical, empty, or pinned at a boundary — there is no variation to rank or compare (+2 more). The difference between slower and faster delivery segments is only 0.2 percentage points, well within expected noise; multiple dimensions show far larger variation, indicating delivery speed is not a driver.

report.executive_summary: Slower-than-average deliveries have an item return rate of **27.4%** versus **27.2%** for faster deliveries, a negligible 0.2‑point difference. Return rates vary strongly by category, peaking at **32.6%** in womenswear, and by platform, with Mytheresa at **32.5%**. Origin country shows Germany at **33.7%**, while destination country variation is modest, highest at Turkey **31.0%}.
report.headline: Slower deliveries do not meaningfully increase item return rates.
report.metric_definition: item return rate — computed as `COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN oi.returned THEN oi.order_item_id END) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_item_id), 0)`; a ratio of two aggregates; (a value-weighted and a count-based reading can differ materially; this reading was chosen automatically); on luxexperience.order_items; over data spanning 2020-07-01 → 2025-06-30.

findings.interpretation: The item return rate shows minimal variation based on delivery speed, with orders delivered slower than average having a return rate of **27.4%** compared to **27.2%** for faster deliveries. This negligible difference suggests that delivery speed is not a primary driver of returns in this dataset.
findings.sql: WITH s AS (SELECT s.order_id, MAX(s.delivery_days) AS delivery_days FROM luxexperience.shipments AS s WHERE NOT s.delivery_days IS NULL GROUP BY s.order_id) SELECT (s.delivery_days > (SELECT AVG(s2.delivery_days) FROM luxexperience.shipments AS s2 WHERE NOT s2.delivery_days IS NULL)) AS segment, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN oi.returned THEN oi.order_item_id END) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_item_id), 0) AS metric_total, COUNT(*) AS n, ROUND((COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN oi.returned THEN oi.order_item_id END) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_item_id), 0)) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 2) AS avg_per_record FROM luxexperience.order_items AS oi JOIN s ON oi.order_id = s.order_id GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
findings.title: Item Return Rate by Delivery-Speed Segment
findings.trust_caveat: every value in this result is identical, empty, or pinned at a boundary — there is no variation to rank or compare

findings.interpretation: Return rates vary significantly by category, ranging from a high of **32.6%** in womenswear to a low of **11.9%** in beauty. The high return rate in womenswear is driven by a substantial volume of **27,424** returned items out of **84,024** total items.
findings.sql: SELECT oi.category AS category, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN oi.returned THEN oi.order_item_id END) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_item_id), 0) AS metric_total, COUNT(*) AS n, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN oi.returned THEN oi.order_item_id END) AS numerator_total, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_item_id) AS denominator_total FROM luxexperience.order_items AS oi GROUP BY oi.category ORDER BY metric_total DESC LIMIT 15
findings.title: Item Return Rate by Category

findings.interpretation: Return rates by origin country show Germany with the highest rate at **33.7%**, while Italy has the lowest at **25.2%**. The spread across these countries is relatively moderate, suggesting regional differences in return behavior.
findings.sql: WITH shipment_origin AS (SELECT s.order_id, MAX(s.origin_country) AS origin_country FROM luxexperience.shipments AS s GROUP BY s.order_id) SELECT shipment_origin.origin_country AS origin_country, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN oi.returned THEN oi.order_item_id END) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_item_id), 0) AS metric_total, COUNT(*) AS n, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN oi.returned THEN oi.order_item_id END) AS numerator_total, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_item_id) AS denominator_total FROM luxexperience.order_items AS oi JOIN shipment_origin ON oi.order_id = shipment_origin.order_id GROUP BY shipment_origin.origin_country ORDER BY metric_total DESC LIMIT 15
findings.title: Item Return Rate by Origin Country
findings.trust_caveat: E1-lexicographic-order: MIN/MAX over text column 'origin_country' compares lexicographically ('10' < '2'). CAST to a numeric type if it stores numbers.

findings.interpretation: Return rates by destination country are tightly clustered, with Turkey showing the highest rate at **31.0%** and other countries following closely. The variation across these destinations is not extreme, indicating a consistent return experience globally.
findings.sql: WITH shipment_destination AS (SELECT s.order_id, MAX(s.destination_country) AS destination_country FROM luxexperience.shipments AS s GROUP BY s.order_id) SELECT shipment_destination.destination_country AS destination_country, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN oi.returned THEN oi.order_item_id END) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_item_id), 0) AS metric_total, COUNT(*) AS n, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN oi.returned THEN oi.order_item_id END) AS numerator_total, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_item_id) AS denominator_total FROM luxexperience.order_items AS oi JOIN shipment_destination ON oi.order_id = shipment_destination.order_id GROUP BY shipment_destination.destination_country ORDER BY metric_total DESC LIMIT 15
findings.title: Item Return Rate by Destination Country
findings.trust_caveat: E1-lexicographic-order: MIN/MAX over text column 'destination_country' compares lexicographically ('10' < '2'). CAST to a numeric type if it stores numbers.

findings.interpretation: Platform return rates show Mytheresa with the highest rate at **32.5%**, while YOOX has the lowest at **20.8%**. This indicates that return behavior is influenced by the platform used, with a notable spread between the highest and lowest performers.
findings.sql: SELECT oi.platform AS platform, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN oi.returned THEN oi.order_item_id END) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_item_id), 0) AS metric_total, COUNT(*) AS n, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN oi.returned THEN oi.order_item_id END) AS numerator_total, COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_item_id) AS denominator_total FROM luxexperience.order_items AS oi GROUP BY oi.platform ORDER BY metric_total DESC LIMIT 15
findings.title: Item Return Rate by Platform

phases.summary: Delivery speed has a negligible impact on returns (**27.4%** vs **27.2%**), while category and platform show significant variance, with womenswear and Mytheresa exhibiting the highest return rates at **32.6%** and **32.5%** respectively.

findings.interpretation: This is a driver/relationship question, so return rate should be compared across delivery-speed groups rather than trended over time. The metric is calculated at order-item grain using order_items.returned; it requires joining luxexperience.order_items oi to luxexperience.shipments s on oi.order_id = s.order_id to obtain delivery_days and ship_date. The canonical Return Rate (by Orders) formula cannot be used because it requires luxexperience.orders, which is not provided in the schema. No profile date range or completeness information was supplied; the stated period is only the range visibly represented by the supplied samples and must be validated against actual data before execution. No status/state column exists in luxexperience.order_items, so no status filter is applied. If orders can have multiple shipment records, shipment-to-order selection/deduplication must be defined before interpreting the relationship.
